title: Pull a specified finite constant model to a geometric point
statement: Work in compatible small-site and coefficient universes. Let $F$ be a normed field with totally disconnected metric topology, put $C_F(P)=C(P,F)$ for profinite $P$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring], and put $F_T=p_T^*C_F$ for every scheme $T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean internal $F_T$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with module inverse images as in [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow T$ be an immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], let $M$ be an $F_S$-module, and fix a pro-etale covering $(v_j:U_j\to S)_j$ with isomorphisms $v_j^*M\cong F_{U_j}\otimes_F P_j$, where each $P_j$ is a finitely presented abstract $F$-module [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Let $x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to T$ be a geometric point with $k$ algebraically closed and image in $i(S)$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. There is a unique factorization $x=i y$ through $S$, and there exist an index $j$, an $S$-morphism $z:s\to U_j$ with $v_jz=y$, an integer $r\geq0$, and an $F$-linear isomorphism $F^r\cong P_j$. Pullback of the specified model and this basis along $z$ gives an isomorphism $y^*M\cong F_s^{\oplus r}$. Under constant sections $\Gamma(s,F_s)=F$, it gives $\Gamma(s,y^*M)\cong F^r$. The conclusion allows $r=0$; neither Noetherianity of $T$ nor completeness of $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 3 and Lemma 4.1(2); agent finite-model lifting at an algebraically closed point (old step 5).

proof.text: The immersion factorization lemma, applied to $i$ and the field-valued point $x$ whose image lies in $i(S)$, gives exactly one $y:s\to S$ with $iy=x$. Its field is the original algebraically closed $k$, so $y$ is a geometric point.

source.place: Tags 01J9 (lemma-characterize-points, preceding discussion) and 01L7 (lemma-immersions-monomorphisms); application of the existing field-point factorization lemma.

proof.text: Put $V_j=s\times_S U_j$ and $w_j:V_j\to s$. The given covering is fpqc with weakly etale members. Arbitrary scheme base change preserves the fpqc covering and each weakly etale member, so $(w_j)_j$ is a covering of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Form its generated covering sieve. The point-cover lemma puts $\mathrm{id}_s$ in this sieve. Membership in a generated sieve means that $\mathrm{id}_s$ factors as $w_j\sigma$ for some original index $j$ and $\sigma:s\to V_j$. Set $z=\operatorname{pr}_{U_j}\sigma$. The fibre-product equation gives $v_jz=y$. This does not assume that $y:s\to S$ is itself an object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tags 022D (topologies.tex, lemma-fpqc (3)), 094U (more-morphisms.tex, lemma-base-change-weakly-etale (2)); 0982 and 098H explain the point-cover property, also proved in AlgClosedFieldSite.lean, id_mem_of_mem_topology_of_iso.

proof.text: Apply the field clause of the scalar finite-free resolutions lemma to the selected finitely presented abstract $F$-module $P_j$. It supplies $r\geq0$ and a basis $p_1,\ldots,p_r$, with $\beta:F^r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j$, $c\mapsto\sum_a c_ap_a$. Write $\lambda_a:P_j\to F$ for the coordinate functions of $\beta^{-1}$. The same clause explicitly includes $P_j=0$ and $r=0$.

source.place: Field specialization in the existing Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-scalar-finite-free-resolutions; Module.finBasis (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Free.lean:334) and Basis.equivFun. No DVR or completeness hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Use the constant-extension interpretation of the specified local model. On $U_j$ the basis gives inverse module maps $B:F_{U_j}^{\oplus r}\to F_{U_j}\otimes_F P_j$ and $A$ in the reverse direction: $B((t_a))=\sum_a t_a\otimes p_a$ and $A(t\otimes p)=(t\lambda_a(p))_a$. Here each $\lambda_a(p)$ acts through constant scalars. These balanced formulas induce maps on the sheafified tensor coequalizer. The identities $\lambda_a(p_b)=\delta_{ab}$ and $p=\sum_a\lambda_a(p)p_a$ give $AB=1$ and $BA=1$. Thus the given model isomorphism followed by $A$ gives $v_j^*M\cong F_{U_j}^{\oplus r}$. For $r=0$ the empty sums are zero and $P_j=0$.

source.place: Section 3, Remark 3.2 and Definition 3.5, printed pp.6--7; agent finite-basis calculation for the ordinary constant-extension local model.

proof.text: Apply $z^*$ to that particular isomorphism. The composition isomorphism identifies $z^*v_j^*M$ with $y^*M$ since $v_jz=y$. The module pullback formula and coefficient isomorphism give $z^*F_{U_j}\cong F_s$: on the relative tensor the maps are $a\otimes b\mapsto a\alpha_z(b)$ and $a\mapsto a\otimes1$. The additive functor $z^*$ preserves the finite biproduct identities $\pi_a\iota_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $\sum_a\iota_a\pi_a=1$; hence $z^*(F_{U_j}^{\oplus r})\cong F_s^{\oplus r}$ with those pulled-back columns. Composing gives the required isomorphism $y^*M\cong F_s^{\oplus r}$ obtained from the specified model and the chosen basis.

source.place: Pullback formula and composition isomorphisms; def-sfb-module-upper-star.md for additivity. Agent regular-module tensor-unit and finite-biproduct calculation.

proof.text: The canonical continuous-function realization identifies $\Gamma(s,F_s)$ with $C(|s|,F)$. Since $|s|$ has one point, value at that point is inverse to the constant-section ring map $F\to\Gamma(s,F_s)$. Taking sections of the preceding basis isomorphism gives $\Gamma(s,y^*M)\cong F^r$: apply sections to its injections and projections; their identities remain $\pi_a\iota_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $\sum_a\iota_a\pi_a=1$, so the coordinates are precisely $r$ copies of $\Gamma(s,F_s)=F$. All maps are linear for these constant scalars. For $r=0$ this is $0\cong F^0$. No step required Noetherianity or completeness.

source.place: Example 3.1, printed p.6: coefficient sheaf U maps to continuous functions on |U|. Agent evaluation at the one-point space and finite-biproduct calculation.

First split of a base-unsplit node; statement unchanged apart from removing doubled backslashes; no new nodes; no repair note; no SGA. Step 1: field-point factorization through an immersion (Stacks 01J9, 01L7) gives a unique y. Step 2: base change of the pro-étale covering along y (Stacks 022D(3) for fpqc, 094U(2) for weakly étale) gives a covering of s_proet. The point-cover lemma puts id_s in the generated sieve, so id_s = w_j σ; with z = pr σ, v_j z = y holds. Step 3: field clause of the Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-scalar-finite-free-resolutions gives a basis, r=0 allowed. Step 4: explicit inverse maps B/A on the constant extension Λ_U⊗_{Λ(*)_U}P_U, balanced, identities check out. Step 5: composition isomorphism, z^*F_U≅F_s by scalar extension of the rank-one module, additivity carries the biproduct. Step 6: continuous-function realization (HRS Example 3.1, p.6, read) gives Γ(s,F_s)=F, and Γ is additive. Edge cases r=0, S empty, empty or infinite covers, nilpotent immersions: all fine. No duplicates (det-pe-wcb-split-cover, lem-pe-finite-coefficient-model-comparison, lem-sfb-normed-locally-free-geometric-matrix-test and others read).
